selection.name: Foundation 1 and the managed closures
selection.rationale: Foundation 1 is the dependency closure of a real textured sprite game: create a native game, receive its lifecycle, expose its graphics device, clear, decode a PNG into a Texture2D, submit a SpriteBatch draw, read the keyboard, exit and destroy deterministically. The selection then grows one dependency-complete closure at a time, in the order NEXT.md records. Some of those closures are pure managed and touch no native route -- the 3D transform types, the bounding volumes, the Curve family and the packed vectors; others reach CNA, as the input surface and the graphics state objects do.

diagnostics.subject: Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Game.OnActivated(Object,EventArgs)
diagnostics.detail: The protected On<Event> methods are the base class's way of raising an event a subclass may intercept before its handlers run. CNA raises the events itself, so there is no place in this projection for a subclass to stand between CNA and the handlers; the event itself is projected and these two are not.

diagnostics.subject: Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Game.ShowMissingRequirementMessage(Exception)
diagnostics.detail: A **protected** virtual (`.method family` in the pinned Game assembly), and one of the raiser-shaped family rather than a member of its own. XNA calls it from inside `Run`'s two catch handlers -- for NoSuitableGraphicsDeviceException and NoAudioHardwareException -- and *rethrows when it answers false*. CNA runs the loop and catches nothing into Lisp: measured against 0.21.0, CNA_GameCallbacks and CNA_GameFrameHooks have load_content, update, draw, unload_content, exiting, initialize, begin_run, end_run, begin_draw and end_draw, and no hook for a run that failed to start. So an override here would never be called. The reason that used to stand said it needed "the CLR exception projection and a platform message box". **CNA has a message box** -- cna_message_box_show_ext and cna_message_box_get_is_supported_ext -- so that half was wrong, and the half that actually blocks it went unmentioned. Its dispatch is also entirely `isinst` on those two exception types, and neither is in the selection.

diagnostics.subject: Microsoft.Xna.Framework.GameComponentCollection.new()
diagnostics.detail: XNA's constructor is public and a standalone collection is legal there, if useless -- a Game makes its own and drives that one. CNA has no route for a collection apart from a game's: `a game owns exactly one component collection, so the collection needs no handle of its own and every route addresses the game's`. So a standalone one is not projected rather than faked.

diagnostics.subject: Microsoft.Xna.Framework.GameWindow.OnActivated()
diagnostics.detail: A protected raiser, and the half that cannot be projected is the half the member exists for: in XNA OnActivated *is* what raises Activated, and a platform window is what calls it. CNA raises, and reaches Lisp only through one callback per subscribed handler, so an override could notify but never suppress. GameWindow is abstract in XNA and these six are its extension point for a platform; this projection is not a platform window.

diagnostics.subject: Microsoft.Xna.Framework.GameWindow.Handle
diagnostics.detail: A System.IntPtr naming the native window. cna_game_window_get_native_handle_ext answers a uint64 rather than refusing, so unlike PresentationParameters.DeviceWindowHandle the number is available -- what is missing is a type to put it in. This projection has no IntPtr, and handing back a bare integer that a consumer can do nothing safe with is not one.

diagnostics.subject: Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics.PresentationParameters.DeviceWindowHandle
diagnostics.detail: A System.IntPtr naming the native window, and this projection has no IntPtr to hand one back in. CNA also refuses the question at this end by design: cna_graphics_device_get_native_window_handle answers CNA_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED after validating the device, and the header gives the reason -- "a device may outlive or precede the window it presents to and answering here would invent an ownership relationship the canonical layer does not have". cna_game_window_get_native_window_ext answers it from the window instead, which is GameWindow.Handle's gap and not this one. The earlier reason named the route `cna_graphics_device_get_device_window_handle`, which does not exist in 0.21.0 under that name.

diagnostics.subject: Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics.GraphicsAdapter.MonitorHandle
diagnostics.detail: A System.IntPtr naming the monitor. CNA refuses the question by design: cna_graphics_adapter_get_native_monitor_handle "reports the native-monitor-handle mapping as unavailable at the stable C boundary" and answers CNA_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED after validating the adapter index. An IntPtr is not a thing this projection has either.

diagnostics.subject: Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics.GraphicsDevice.Present(Nullable`1,Nullable`1,IntPtr)
diagnostics.detail: Needs Nullable<Rectangle> and IntPtr, neither of which is projected -- and there is no route either: cna_graphics_device_present takes the device and nothing else, so the source rectangle, destination rectangle and override window have nowhere to go. The no-argument Present is complete.

diagnostics.subject: Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics.GraphicsDevice.ResourceDestroyed
diagnostics.detail: As ResourceCreated, from the other end, and blocked the same two ways. CNA_ResourceDestroyedEventInfo carries a callback-scoped name and a `has_tag` boolean -- the header: "the canonical `System::Object*` tag is caller-owned native state, so it is reported as presence only" -- and ResourceDestroyedEventArgs is not in the selection. Its Name could be answered; its Tag could not, and half an event args under the event's name would be worse than the absence.

diagnostics.subject: Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics.GraphicsDevice.ResourceCreated
diagnostics.detail: Two blockers, either one sufficient. **CNA reports presence, not a resource**: CNA_ResourceCreatedEventInfo carries `has_resource` and nothing else, and the header says why -- "the canonical event is raised from the graphics-resource base constructor, so the reported object is still under construction: its concrete type does not exist yet and no member of it can be queried. The C event therefore reports only that a resource was supplied, and no native object pointer crosses the ABI." And **ResourceCreatedEventArgs is not in the selection**, so there is no type to hand a resource in even if one crossed. The earlier reason said this needed "a decision about what object a handler is handed"; there is nothing to hand.

diagnostics.subject: Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics.Effect.OnApply()
diagnostics.detail: A protected-internal virtual (`.method famorassem`) that XNA calls from inside EffectPass.Apply, so a subclass can adjust parameters immediately before the pass is applied. CNA applies a pass in one route -- cna_effect_pass_apply(pass) takes the pass and nothing else -- with no callback into managed code in the middle, so an override here would never be called. The same shape as ContentManager.ReadAsset: a hook needs somewhere to be called from. The reason that used to stand added "and returning true from it cancels the pass". **In the pinned assembly OnApply returns `void`** and cancels nothing; Effect's own body is a single `ret`. That was a claim about XNA taken from somewhere other than XNA.

diagnostics.subject: Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics.EffectParameter.GetValueTexture3D()
diagnostics.detail: Needs Texture3D, which is neither projected nor in the selection. The CNA route would take it as its third texture-type identity, so the gap is the type.

diagnostics.subject: Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics.DirectionalLight.new(EffectParameter,EffectParameter,EffectParameter,DirectionalLight)
diagnostics.detail: XNA's constructor takes three EffectParameters and a DirectionalLight to copy from, which is how the stock effects wire their own lights up: the light *is* the three parameters, and writing it writes them. A program does not build one -- it reaches DirectionalLight through BasicEffect.DirectionalLight0 and its two siblings, which are complete. **cna_directional_light_create does exist**, and it is not this constructor: it takes no arguments and, in the header's words, "creates an owned default disabled DirectionalLight" with no parameters behind it. The wiring is the member, and CNA's route cannot express it.

diagnostics.subject: Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Media.Song.Artist
diagnostics.detail: Needs Artist, which is neither projected nor in the selection: it is a media-library entity whose CNA routes are in media_library.h, and cna_song_get_artist reports it unavailable for a song created from a file path -- the only kind this closure can make, measured on all three admitted ABIs. Selecting the four library types to satisfy this member and its two siblings would add 53 members nothing here could exercise, which is the reason MediaLibrary was not the closure chosen.
